translations.translatedText: # Sunday 10.09.2017 (radio)
Ditching harms lakes and rivers. Water levels are now high. Olli Heikkonen has received the Einari Vuorela poetry prize. Finland's jubilee year was visible at a women's running event in Paris.
## Ditching forests and bogs is harmful to waters
![A ditch in a drained bog](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-5426180)
Open image viewer
A ditch in a drained bog. Photo: Eijaleena Martikainen / Yle

Ditching forests is more harmful than was known. More nutrients end up from ditches in lakes, for example, than was thought. Studies show that many times more nitrogen and phosphorus get into waters compared with earlier calculations. There are especially large emissions when ditches are dug in a bog. Now it is known that the emissions get worse as the years pass. The result surprised the researchers.

Clear-cutting of forests increases nutrient emissions into waters through ditches. That is why researchers recommend continuous-cover forestry. Then the soil is not disturbed as harshly as in clear-cutting.
The matter was studied by the Natural Resources Institute Finland and the Finnish Environment Institute. A quarter of Finland's forest area has been ditched.
## Lake and river levels are now high
![The Kolera basin at Helsinki Market Square.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-8507488)
Open image viewer
This is how high the water level was in Helsinki's Kolera basin two years ago. Photo: Jani Saikko / Yle
Heavy rains are now raising the level of rivers and lakes in almost the whole country.
Water levels are rising especially in Kainuu and North Ostrobothnia. It has rained most on the Iisalmi route of the Vuoksi water system, in Kainuu and on the Iijoki river. Low-lying areas may flood.
In places, lake levels are as much as half a metre higher than usual.
## Olli Heikkonen received the Einari Vuorela poetry prize
![Poet Olli Heikkonen.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9823979)
Open image viewer
Nature is strongly present in all of Olli Heikkonen's works. Photo: Heini Lehväslaiho
The poet Olli Heikkonen has received Finland's biggest poetry prize. The Einari Vuorela poetry prize is awarded every third (3) year. The prize is 8,500 euros.

52-year-old Olli Heikkonen received the prize for the poetry book Teoria kaikkein pienimmästä (Theory of the Very Smallest). It is Heikkonen's fourth (4) poetry collection. The jury says that the work has a delicious collision of nature and culture. The tone of the prize-winning book is described as serious humour.
Olli Heikkonen has won prizes before. He received the Helsingin Sanomat literature prize in 2000. Then Heikkonen's work Jakutian aurinko (The Sun of Yakutia) won the prize.
## Daughters of the North in Paris
![There was nothing to complain about in the scenery and atmosphere of the Finland 100 run.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-9825132)
Open image viewer
There was nothing to complain about in the scenery and atmosphere of the Finland 100 run.  Photo: Juha Nurminen
Europe's largest women's running event has been held in Paris. The race is held every year. This time the La Parisienne event also had a Finnish touch.

A blue-and-white team of over a hundred (100) Finnish women took part in the race in honour of Finland's jubilee year. The group of runners was called Pohjolan tyttäret (Daughters of the North). Many came to the race from far away, and for not everyone was running the main thing. The participants say that Finns living abroad have a great need to celebrate 100-year-old Finland and their own roots. Among the spectators there were many Finnish families living abroad - and also Santa Claus.
The event had more than 30,000 runners in total.
